text:
alex: Heads up — starting the orders schema change (add shard_key) in 30m. planning a canary on 5% of traffic first, then traffic-split to 25% if metrics look good. Deploy window 02:00-04:00 UTC. pinging @deploy-bot to schedule and @oncall-sre for lock-watch.
priya: Thanks. what's the backfill approach? full-table backfill or incremental? worried about long-running row locks.
danielle: incremental backfill with batching and restartability. backfill job will use batch_size=1000 and sleep_ms=200 between batches. will stream to new column via rewrite job.
alex: SQL for DDL is just ADD COLUMN NULLABLE, then backfill + set NOT NULL in follow-up migration. snippet:
```sql
ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN shard_key varchar(32);
-- backfill job reads batches, writes shard_key via UPDATE
```
deploy-bot: scheduled migration job orders.add_shard_key at 2025-05-10T02:00:00Z (thread=1742003333). canary route created: orders-service@canary-5pct. Log: canary task will run migration binary v1.8.4.
priya: @danielle how will we detect lock escalation? can we have an automatic hold when any table-level lock > 10s or row lock retries spike 3x p50->p95?
danielle: yes. backfill exposes metrics: backfill.batch_duration_ms, db.row_lock_wait_ms. we'll gate canary to abort if p95 lock_wait > 2000ms for 3 consecutive minutes.
oncall-sre: i'll add a lockwatcher that watches pg_stat_activity and emits deploybot alert. if lock queue length > 5 or deadlocks, we hit the abort path. also set DB connections for backfill to low priority role.
sam: for rollback — what's the exact plan? if canary fails, do we auto-rollback to previous model + pin schema version? manual rollback required?
alex: rollout policy: 1) canary 5% 20m observation; 2) if metrics within SLO, split to 25% for 10m; 3) full rollout. abort triggers -> deploy-bot blocks further waves and posts rollback recommendation. rollback is manual for data-affecting changes (we won't DROP column). we will revert service image if behavioral regressions; schema can stay (it's additive) but we'll pause backfill and revert traffic split.
priya: add explicit pin command please so release engineers can pin quickly.
deploy-bot: pin command available: `/deploy pin-version orders-service 1.12.3 --reason "schema canary fail"` . also `deploy-bot hold thread 1742003333` will stop further waves.
danielle: will also expose a migration progress endpoint `/migration/orders/shard_key/status` returning {"applied_batches": 123, "errors": 0, "last_batch_ms": 412}. ops can inspect before deciding rollback.
alex: good. one more: feature-flag the new routing by shard_key so we can toggle for small user cohorts if we need a narrower rollback.
priya: noted. i'll be watching p99 write latency and error rate, plus the backfill metrics. i'll post checkpoints at +5m, +15m, +25m during canary.
oncall-sre: i'll be on-call at 02:00. if I see lock_watch alerts i'll call abort and post the reason. :thumbsup:
sam: acknowledged. I'll prepare release notes blurb: "Add shard_key to orders (nullable). Incremental backfill with safety gates. Can reclaim if lock escalation observed."
